attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No candidate generator is known for which min_Pi sum_B C_{R_B}(OR-SAT_B) can be proved at N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} in general circuits.
steps: Let M=N^q and let G_N(x) output the M formulas y_1(x),...,y_M(x) of length L=(log N)^d using N^{rho+o(1)} gates.
Fix a partition Pi of [M]. For each block B, define R_B as the set of generated tuples y_B(x) and choose a smallest circuit Q_B agreeing with OR_{j in B} SAT(y_j) on R_B.
Compose one copy of G_N with all Q_B circuits, wire each Q_B to its block tuple, and OR the block answers. This computes H_N exactly.
The resulting size is N^{rho+o(1)}+sum_B C_{R_B}(OR-SAT_B)+O(|Pi|), proving the shared-generator cover upper bound.
For singleton blocks, if SAT has L^c-size circuits, then each block cost is at most L^c, giving C(H_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}+N^qL^c and hence the target-preserving contradiction when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
Therefore a valid source lower bound must simultaneously rule out all nonuniform semantic block covers; otherwise the cover is an explicit falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation supplies conditional transfer and sharp upper-bound obstructions only. Proving the required semantic block-cover lower bound for one explicit H_N appears at least as hard as a non-natural general-circuit lower bound and is not a proof of P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: Shared-Generator Semantic Block-Cover Gate

assumptions: Circuit size is nonuniform Boolean circuit size with fan-in two unless stated otherwise.
The generator has no target advice depending on a hypothetical SAT circuit beyond its fixed nonuniform description for length N.
The source lower bound is an eventually-all-N lower bound for the explicit carrier H_N, not merely an infinitely-often or average-case statement.
The range-restricted block circuits are allowed arbitrary nonuniform advice for length N; hence this is a strong falsifier gate for source lower bounds.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{1<=j<=M} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)), with input length N, M=N^q, query length L(N)=(log N)^d, and a nonuniform generator circuit G_N of size N^{rho+o(1)} outputting all query strings.
target object: SAT restricted to formulas of length L(N), with the target consequence SAT notin P/poly if the bridge contradicts every fixed polynomial-size SAT circuit family.
controlled interface: substitute a candidate SAT_L circuit only at generated query positions, and separately audit every block predicate that may exploit the realized tuple range of the generator.

target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon and rho<1+epsilon, with d>1 or a certified lookup-safety condition, so the carrier upper bound from SAT circuits is below the claimed N^{1+epsilon} source threshold.
For a partition Pi of [M], R_B={ (G_{N,j}(x))_{j in B}: x in {0,1}^N } is the realized tuple range of block B.
C_{R_B}(OR-SAT_B) is the minimum circuit size of a predicate Q_B on |B| generated formulas that agrees with OR_{j in B} SAT(y_j) on all tuples in R_B; behavior outside R_B is irrelevant.
A shared-generator block cover has cost C(G_N)+sum_{B in Pi} C_{R_B}(OR-SAT_B)+O(|Pi|).

Feature-cover cost is C(G_N shared parts)+sum_B(C(A_B)+C(D_B))+O(|Pi|).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The route must prove a genuine anti-concentration condition, such as Delta <= N^{-A}/polylog(N), for the actual coefficients used by the separator. Without it, dominated halfspaces have exponentially small density.
steps: Model the proposed lower-bound certificate as H_N(f)=1[sum_z a_z(-1)^{f(z)}>=tau] with coefficients generated in poly(N) time.
Under a uniformly random truth table F, replace bits by independent signs X_z=(-1)^{F(z)} and normalize L=sum_z a_z X_z by sigma.
Apply Berry-Esseen: the distribution of L/sigma differs from a standard Gaussian by at most C_BE Delta.
If tau/sigma<=c sqrt(ln N) and Delta is below the polynomial Gaussian tail, infer density at least N^{-A}/2.
Poly(N)-time coefficient generation and rational comparison give constructivity of H_N.
The promised rejection of all SIZE(m^k) truth tables gives usefulness; hence H_N is a natural property and a PRF distinguisher.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only audits a class of proof objects. It does not construct a SAT separator, does not prove SAT notin SIZE(m^k), and gives no direct evidence for P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: regular halfspace naturalization gate

assumptions: N=2^m, coefficients are rationals of poly(N) bit complexity, and H_N is decidable in poly(N) time from the full truth table.
Under a uniform random Boolean function F, the signs (-1)^{F(z)} are independent Rademacher variables.
Let T=tau/sigma. For fixed c and A with A>c^2/2, assume T<=c sqrt(ln N) and Delta <= (2 C_BE)^{-1} N^{-A} for all large N.
Usefulness is syntactic: every m-input circuit of size m^k has truth table rejected by this same H_N.
definitions: source object: an explicit regular weighted halfspace H_N(f)=1[sum_z a_z (-1)^{f(z)} >= tau] over the N=2^m truth-table bits, proposed as a SAT_m separator.
target object: a Razborov-Rudich natural property useful against SIZE(m^k) truth tables with density at least N^{-A} and poly(N)-time decidability.
controlled interface: coefficient generator plus threshold plus proof that H_N(SAT_m)=1 and H_N(g)=0 for every g computed by circuits of size m^k.

target-preserving condition: the same explicit halfspace, with no advice-dependent reweighting, must reject the entire target circuit class and have anti-concentration under the uniform random truth table.
regularity parameter: sigma^2=sum_z a_z^2 and Delta=max_z |a_z|/sigma.

equations.label: berry_esseen_tail

equations.valid_when: Applies after the Gaussian tail is polynomially larger than the Berry-Esseen error and N is sufficiently large.

This is a falsifier for degree-only and normalized-threshold-only naturalization claims, not for regular halfspaces.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation only supplies an upper-bound cap. For epsilon<=alpha_V it gives no source soundness, and constructing a sparse non-natural high-MCSP certificate family remains open.
steps: Fix an accepted certificate y at length m and let T_y be the emitted table of N=2^m bits.
Choose a block length B=2^{lambda m}; hardwire V's configuration at the start of each of the N/B blocks.
The checkpoint advice has size 2^{(1-lambda+sigma)m+o(m)} because there are 2^{(1-lambda)m} blocks and each configuration has 2^{sigma m+o(m)} bits.
On an m-bit input index i, a circuit selects the checkpoint for i's block and replays at most B outputs, costing 2^{tau_V(lambda)m+o(m)} gates.
Thus C(T_y) is bounded by 2^{max{1-lambda+sigma,tau_V(lambda)}m+o(m)} for every lambda, and optimizing gives alpha_V.
For polynomial-space linear replay, lambda=1/2 gives C(T_y)<=2^{m/2+o(m)}, contradicting any asserted MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m} with epsilon>1/2.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This refutes invalid carriers and preserves a valid conditional transfer, but it does not construct the needed uniform no-side MCSP certificates and therefore does not prove P != NP.

assumptions: V deterministically emits the truth table in a fixed order and its transition/replay procedure is uniform in m.
For every accepted certificate y, source soundness asserts general Boolean circuit complexity C(T_y)>2^{epsilon m}.
A block-start configuration can be hardwired into a circuit and selected by the high-order bits of the input index.
The replay profile tau_V(lambda) is certified without using nonuniform advice depending on the target input length beyond the hardwired checkpoints.
definitions: source object: uniform short-certificate sequential MCSP carrier V={V_m} emitting truth tables T_y of length N=2^m from certificates |y|=O(m).
target object: an E language L whose length-n slices avoid SIZE(2^{delta n}) for a fixed delta>0 after padding transfer.
controlled interface: exhaustive E-time canonicalization of accepted certificates plus MCSP no-side soundness C(T_y)>2^{epsilon m} on kappa-dense source lengths.

target-preserving condition: the verifier is uniform, certificates have O(m) bits, source lengths are kappa-dense below target lengths, and no nonuniform selector, salt-density repair, or low-local decoder is used.
sigma is the configuration-entropy exponent: a stored configuration has 2^{sigma m+o(m)} bits.
tau_V(lambda) is the replay exponent for producing a block of 2^{lambda m} outputs from one stored configuration.
alpha_V is an unconditional nonuniform circuit upper-bound cap for every emitted table in this verifier model.

equations.label: checkpoint_upper
equations.valid_when: Valid when V emits the table sequentially from stored configurations and a 2^{lambda m}-output replay circuit can be unrolled uniformly.

equations.label: optimized_cap
equations.valid_when: Applies after the replay profile is fixed independently of the certificate and checkpoint descriptions are hardwired nonuniformly into the test circuit.

equations.label: linear_replay_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid for ordinary one-pass polynomial-space emitters whose next-output simulation costs one step per emitted bit.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the source claims epsilon>alpha_V under its declared sigma and tau_V, the MCSP no-side soundness is false; if tau_V is undeclared, the source is not yet a valid bridge object.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-level obstruction lemma: it proves a quantitative upper-bound falsifier for proposed MCSP certificate sources before applying the carrier-to-E extraction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let V be a uniform short-certificate sequential MCSP carrier. On certificate y of length O(m), V emits an N=2^m bit truth table T_y using configurations of size at most 2^{sigma m+o(m)} bits. If tau_V(lambda) is the circuit-size exponent needed to replay 2^{lambda m} consecutive outputs from a stored configuration, then every accepted T_y has circuit complexity at most 2^{alpha_V m+o(m)}, where alpha_V=inf_lambda max{1-lambda+sigma,tau_V(lambda)}. Thus a claimed MCSP no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m} is valid only when epsilon<=alpha_V; epsilon>alpha_V is a route falsifier.

assumptions: The emitted table length is N=2^m and output positions are visited in lexicographic order.
A circuit may hardwire one checkpoint per block and simulate within the selected block.
definitions: source model: O(m)-bit certificates, poly(m)-bit configurations, sequential truth-table emission, no indexed restart oracle.
target model: general fan-in two Boolean circuits measured against MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
barrier status: the corollary is a relativizing upper-bound obstruction, not a nonrelativizing lower-bound proof.

equations.label: polyspace_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when configuration size is subexponential and replaying a block has cost proportional to the block length.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A candidate with hidden random access, compressed local decoding, or advice-aided checkpoint selection falls outside the stated source model and must be audited separately.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Refutes overstrong sequential-certificate proposals while leaving epsilon<=1/2 source construction open.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a polynomial-space one-pass emitter with linear replay cost, every accepted N=2^m bit table has circuits of size 2^{m/2+o(m)}. Therefore no such source can soundly certify GapMCSP no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m} for any epsilon>1/2.

assumptions: The canonical search over O(m)-bit certificates and verification time 2^{O(m)} stays within E.
Every accepted certificate is sound; lexicographic choice is used only for uniformity, not for soundness.
No natural-property largeness is introduced by salt or dense acceptance.
definitions: source model: accepted certificates at infinitely many kappa-dense source lengths m, all producing high-MCSP truth tables.
target class: E against nonuniform SIZE(2^{delta n}) circuits on all sufficiently large input lengths.
padding convention: for each target length n choose a certified source length m in [n/kappa,n] and fix the remaining input bits.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Conditional extraction theorem with the cap constraint explicitly attached to the source side.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a uniform short-certificate MCSP carrier is kappa-dense, E-canonicalizable, sound at threshold 2^{epsilon m}, and survives the checkpoint cap epsilon<=alpha_V, then it yields an E language requiring SIZE(2^{delta n}) circuits for every delta<epsilon/kappa. This is a valid route bridge, not a proof of P != NP without constructing the source.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every plausible short-certificate source either has alpha_V=0, requires nonuniform witness selection, or uses salt/local decoding that triggers the listed falsifier conditions.

The E lower-bound transfer remains valid as delta<epsilon/kappa, but only after the source survives epsilon<=alpha_V and uniform canonicalization.
O(m)-certificate exhaustive search is enough for E explicitness; nonuniform witness selection and superlinear certificates are still quarantined.
Block checkpointing gives alpha_V=inf_lambda max{1-lambda+sigma,tau_V(lambda)} and refutes source thresholds above that value.

falsifier: any declared source with alpha_V<epsilon cannot be a sound no-side GapMCSP carrier.
